title: Definite vs partitive, and pas de

items.fullSentence: Chaque matin, je bois du café.

whyWrong.le: le café means coffee in general; drinking 'some' takes du.
whyWrong.un: un café means 'a coffee' (a cup); for an amount use du.
whyWrong.de la: café is masculine — du, not de la.

items.fullSentence: Elle mange de la salade tous les midis.

whyWrong.la: la salade means salad in general; eating 'some' takes de la.
whyWrong.une: une salade means a whole salad; for an amount use de la.
whyWrong.du: salade is feminine — de la, not du.

whyWrong.l': l'eau means 'the water'; asking for 'some' takes de l'.
whyWrong.du: eau is feminine and starts with a vowel — de l', not du.
whyWrong.de la: Before a vowel, de la elides to de l'.

items.fullSentence: Il y a des oranges sur la table.
items.sentenceTrans: There are some oranges on the table.

whyWrong.les: les oranges means the specific oranges; 'some' is des.
whyWrong.de les: de + les always contracts to des.
whyWrong.de: In this affirmative sentence a plural count noun takes des, not bare de.

whyWrong.de la: After adorer you use the definite article — la pizza, not the partitive.
whyWrong.du: pizza is feminine, and after adorer you need la.
whyWrong.une: adorer takes the general 'la pizza', not 'a pizza'.

whyWrong.de la: huile starts with a vowel — de la elides to de l'.
whyWrong.du: huile is feminine — de l', not du.
whyWrong.une: Here you add 'some' oil, an amount, so de l'.

items.sentenceBefore: J'aime la bière, mais ce soir je bois
items.fullSentence: J'aime la bière, mais ce soir je bois du vin.
items.sentenceTrans: I like beer, but tonight I'm drinking (some) wine.

whyWrong.le: le vin means wine in general; drinking 'some' takes du.
whyWrong.de la: vin is masculine — du, not de la.
whyWrong.un: un vin means 'a wine' (a glass or type); for an amount use du.

items.fullSentence: Elle ne mange pas de viande.

whyWrong.de la: After a negative, the partitive de la becomes plain de.
whyWrong.du: After a negative, du becomes de.
whyWrong.pas de la: The 'pas' is already in the sentence; the blank is just de.

items.fullSentence: Il ne boit pas d'eau — seulement du jus.
items.sentenceTrans: He doesn't drink water — only juice.

whyWrong.de: Before a vowel, de elides to d'.
whyWrong.de l': After a negative the partitive drops to d', not de l'.
whyWrong.pas d': The 'pas' is already there; the blank is just d'.

items.fullSentence: — C'est du café ? — Non, ce n'est pas du café — c'est du thé.
items.sentenceTrans: — Is it coffee? — No, it's not coffee — it's tea.

whyWrong.ce n'est pas de: The pas → de rule applies to verbs like boire/manger/prendre — after être the partitive is retained: ce n'est pas du café.
whyWrong.il n'y a pas de: That means 'there isn't any'; here we're saying 'it isn't coffee'.
whyWrong.ce n'est pas de la: café is masculine — du, not de la.
